chunks: “Wudu (ablution) after ghusl (ritual bath) is a bid'ah.” The correct approach here also is what we mentioned regarding the first two reports alike. As for the other ghusls, taharah must be performed before them, and the reports that have come stating that there is no wudu in them are such as:
(397) 88 — What Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad, from his grandfather Ibrahim ibn Muhammad:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hamdani wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith عليه السلام asking him about wudu for salat in the ghusl of Friday, and he wrote: “There is no wudu for salat in the ghusl of the day of Friday, nor in any other.”
(398) 89 And similarly what Sa'd also narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a man who performs ghusl from his janabah, or on Friday, or on the day of 'Eid: is wudu required of him before that or after it? He said: “No. It is not upon him before nor after; the ghusl has sufficed him. And the woman is the same in that: when she performs ghusl from hayd or other than that, then there is no wudu upon her, neither before nor after, and the ghusl has sufficed her.”

(399) 90 And similarly what Sa'd narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from a man, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performs ghusl for Friday or for something else, does it suffice him in place of wudu? Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: “And what wudu is purer than ghusl?”

So the meaning of these reports is that when these ghusls, or some of them, are combined with ghusl al-janabah, then wudu falls away. But when these ghusls, or some of them, are performed separately from ghusl al-janabah, then wudu is obligatory before them, as indicated by what has preceded from his statement عليه السلام: “Every ghusl is preceded by wudu except ghusl al-janabah.” And what further clarifies that is:
(400) 91 What Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Hariz, or from one who narrated it from him, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: The people of Kufah narrate from 'Ali عليه السلام that he used to command wudu before ghusl from janabah. He said: “They have lied against 'Ali عليه السلام. They did not find that in the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام. Allah, Most High, said:
“And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves.”

key_terms.اَلطَّهَارَةِ: ritual purity or purification, mentioned as needing to precede certain ghusls
key_terms.اَلْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath), the major purification central to the legal ruling here
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification discussed as being required or not before certain ghusls
key_terms.بِدْعَةٌ: an innovation, used here for performing wudu after ghusl
key_terms.جُنُبًا: in a state of janabah, the Quranic term cited concerning major ritual impurity
key_terms.حَيْضٍ: menstruation, one of the causes for a woman's ghusl mentioned in the report
key_terms.غُسْلِ اَلْجَنَابَةِ: the ghusl of janabah, treated here as distinct from other ghusls in its ruling regarding wudu
key_terms.يَوْمِ اَلْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, referring to the recommended ghusl performed then

ai.seo_question: Does ghusl replace wudu in Shia hadith, especially for janabah and Friday ghusl?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling of wudu in relation to ghusl, especially ghusl al-janabah and other ritual baths such as Friday and 'Eid ghusl. It cites several reports and concludes that wudu is not required with ghusl al-janabah, while other ghusls are interpreted in light of earlier reports requiring wudu when they are performed independently.
